## Putting methods to the test

Shared datasets and clearly defined tasks can show how methods perform on the questions that matter in drug development. We are building an open collection that makes those comparisons reproducible, useful, and easy to discuss across the field.

[Suggest a benchmark problem](https://github.com/AIML-SIG/pmx_benchmarks/issues/new){.btn .btn-primary .btn-lg} [Explore the scope](scope.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary .btn-lg}

:::

::: {.home-section}

## The vision

Methods papers in pharmacometrics often use proprietary datasets or simulations designed for one method. When the data, questions, and evaluation criteria differ between papers, it is difficult to compare results. Simulations can also miss the irregular sampling, missing data, and other challenges encountered in practice, leaving method developers without shared examples of the problems they need to solve.

We aim to collect benchmarks with a clear pharmacometric question, documented data and assumptions, defined tasks and metrics, and a justified train/test split. Shared benchmarks can make research easier to compare and help direct new methods toward practical drug-development decisions.

The Benchmarking Datasets Working Group of the AI/ML SIG is developing this collection, with hosting under ISoP planned. Participation is open to the wider pharmacometrics community.

:::

::: {.home-section}

## Two ways to build a benchmark

::: {.home-grid}

::: {.home-card}

### Generic benchmarks

Focused cases for method comparison, teaching, or evaluating automated modeling workflows. A small synthetic dataset that isolates sparse sampling, mixed dosing, or a covariate challenge can be valuable.

[See Goal 1 criteria](scope.qmd#goal-1-generic-benchmarks)

:::

::: {.home-card}

### Grand challenges

Realistic, consequential drug-development problems that current methods struggle to address. These are intended for deeper scientific review and may support future community challenges.

[See Goal 2 criteria](scope.qmd#goal-2-grand-challenges)

:::

:::

:::

::: {.home-section}

## How you can get involved

::: {.home-grid .home-grid-three}

::: {.home-card}

### 1. Bring a problem

Tell us about a pharmacometric decision that deserves a better benchmark. An idea is enough to start; you do not need to have a dataset ready.

[Open a discussion issue](https://github.com/AIML-SIG/pmx_benchmarks/issues/new)

:::

::: {.home-card}

### 2. Contribute a dataset

Submit a documented dataset with a defined task, metric, and train/test split. Synthetic datasets and focused cases are welcome.

[Read the submission guide](submission-guide.qmd)

:::

::: {.home-card}

### 3. Help shape the work

Offer to review a submission, help define useful evaluation tasks, or try the reference example and tell us what is missing.

[Get in touch](contact.qmd)

:::

:::

:::
